issues.description: Class Stock: the problem statement UML and the solution implementation declare/implement a method named emptyStock(), but the template Stock class exposes the same operation under the different identifier clearInventory(). This naming mismatch (emptyStock() vs clearInventory()) is a real API inconsistency across artifacts and can confuse students: they may implement or call emptyStock() following the UML/solution while the provided starter code only offers clearInventory(), causing compilation errors or unexpected test failures.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fixes (choose one):
1) Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (signature: public void emptyStock()) so it matches the UML and solution. Update any internal callers. OR
2) Add a public void emptyStock() method to the template that simply calls existing clearInventory(), preserving the current template while providing the API students expect. OR
3) If clearInventory() is the intended name, update the problem statement UML and the solution to reference clearInventory() instead. Ensure all references (docs, tests, and code) use the same identifier.
